BINANCE SEES $3.5 BILLION IN OUTFLOWS AFTER RECORD $6.3 BILLION HACK Binance recorded more than $3.5 billion in net outflows Sunday, according to DefiLlama, after resuming withdrawals following a $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft. The exchange says it has replaced 95% of stolen assets, with withdrawals now stabilizing. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacking group, although President Trump said the country’s involvement remains uncertain.

LIBERMAN BACKS EISENKOT, RULES OUT COALITION WITH NETANYAHU Israeli opposition leader Avigdor Liberman reportedly said his party will recommend Gadi Eisenkot to lead the next government. Liberman reiterated that Benjamin Netanyahu must leave office, ruling out joining a coalition with him even under a rotating premiership. He also said Yair Lapid wants to become Speaker of the Knesset and pledged support for his candidacy.

MIZUHO REITERATES $165 TARGET ON STRATEGY ($MSTR ) Mizuho maintained its Outperform rating and $165 price target on Strategy following its Q3 2026 earnings call. Analyst Dan Dolev highlighted a stronger balance sheet, with 848,517 BTC held, net leverage falling to 2.4% from 8.4%, and $5.1 billion in USD assets covering 3.4 years of dividends and interest. However, Bitcoin per share has declined 3.7% year to date, raising dilution concerns.

APPLE'S PREMIUM VALUATION LEAVES LITTLE ROOM FOR ERROR: OPPENHEIMER Oppenheimer reiterated its Perform rating on Apple ($AAPL ) ahead of earnings, warning that its elevated valuation limits upside. The firm forecasts Q4 revenue of $112.9 billion and EPS of $1.96, both below consensus. Its 2027 EPS estimate of $8.91 is 7% below expectations, reflecting slowing iPhone growth, rising memory costs and Services headwinds. TRUMP SIGNALS POSSIBLE PARDONS FOR ALLIES, INCLUDING ELON MUSK President Trump suggested he could pardon political allies, including Elon Musk, if they face legal action. "I would do it if I needed to," Trump said in a Pod Force One interview, referencing his January 6 pardons. The remarks come as Democrats threaten investigations into the Trump administration if they regain control of Congress in Tuesday's midterms.

MUSK THROTTLES GROK BOT AS AI COSTS BECOME UNSUSTAINABLE Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX intentionally restricted Grok Bot usage over Halloween weekend, citing operating costs that were “unsustainably high relative to revenue.” Some users reported their weekly usage jumping from 50% to 100% without additional activity. The restrictions come despite SpaceX reporting that AI accounts for 52% of company income, with its Super Intelligence division generating $431 million in profit.

US DATA CENTER CONSTRUCTION SURGES AT RECORD PACE DESPITE SPENDING SLUMP US construction spending fell 1.9% in September, but underlying momentum remains strong, supported by AI infrastructure investment. Data center construction surged at a record 211% quarterly annualized pace, with monthly growth of 8–10% over the past four months. POWER OUTAGE HITS DOWNTOWN WASHINGTON AHEAD OF ELECTION DAY More than 1,100 customers lost power in Washington, D.C., just blocks from the White House, on the eve of the US midterm elections. Utility provider Pepco reports 1,176 affected customers, with a substation failure identified as the probable cause. Outages are concentrated in Foggy Bottom, home to the State Department.

US–IRAN BREAKTHROUGH REPORTED, BUT CAUTION WARRANTED Al-Jadeed reports a breakthrough in US–Iran negotiations, claiming Qatari mediation successfully resolved procedural obstacles. However, the report remains unconfirmed by major international news agencies, and previous claims of diplomatic breakthroughs have proven inaccurate. No official agreement or substantive details have been announced.
